mechaber/1:main: THE COMMANDMENT TO KNEAD THE MATZAH OF THE EVE OF PESACH: ONE SECTION It is customary to not knead Matzot Mitzvah on the eve of Pesach until after the sixth hour, as this was the time when the Pesach offering was offered. When the 14th [of Nissan] falls out on Shabbos, one should knead on the eve of Shabbos after the sixth hour.
baer-heitev/1:_: Six hours. And a half. So wrote Bach and Taz and Kaf HaChayyim, not like Magen Avraham. Bach wrote one does not fulfill with matzah baked thirty days before, even if made for Pesach, and most poskim disagree — see Kaf HaChayyim. The meticulous practice to bake everything before Pesach so that if something chametz becomes mixed it will be nullified; and so practiced Maharshal. Magen Avraham wrote and it is obvious that when baked before Pesach and mixed in kneading, it is permitted afterward to cook the matzot on Pesach — for otherwise even to eat them plain is forbidden, unlike Eshel Avraham siman 453. Maharil wrote that some bake during the festival to eat fresh matzot every day; and Taz wrote it is not proper to do so — see there his reason; and so Acharonim. Matat Moshe wrote: the baker on the night of Yom Tov may not bake doubtful matzot; and likewise forbidden to bake on the first night for the second night; however if he baked while still day on the first night he may say "I eat today warm bread" and may bake others on the first night, and what he baked while still day he hides for the second night — see above siman 437 seif 7. If dough was kneaded close to nightfall and he did not manage to bake it until nightfall, it is permitted to bake it on Yom Tov so it not chametz — Magen Avraham.
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (s.k. 1) After etc. As Tosafot wrote Pesachim daf 5 and Yoma. For in Pesachim Rava said: this that is written "only on the first day you shall rest" — necessarily means from Yom Tov from midday, as written "you shall not slaughter on chametz the blood of my sacrifice" — youremeans do not slaughter the Pesach while chametz still exists; and he concludes this is the time of slaughtering the Pesach. Proven that from the time of slaughtering the Pesach there is a positive commandment of "you shall rest" — meaning from Yom Tov from midday. Rashba challenged in Tosafot s.v. lo tishchat etc.: behold the time of slaughtering the Pesach is after the tamid, and the tamid slaughtered before midday is invalid; if so necessarily since one must delay the Pesach after the tamid, slaughtering the Pesach is not immediately after midday. And answer: since b'dieved if he slaughtered the Pesach before the tamid it is valid, it is properly called midday the time of slaughtering the Pesach — end quote; and still difficult: behold the time of slaughtering is from six and a half. And necessarily must say as we say in Yoma daf 28: in truth its time begins at seven; however the walls of the Temple were wide and it was impossible to determine midday precisely in the shadow of the walls until six and a half; and so Rashi wrote there in Pesachim.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: In Uganda, the D.C. page from the host and above:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ג: Tur wrote etc. everything before Pesach etc. — excluding those who bake on the night of the first Yom Tov and on the second Yom Tov; and see there the reason of the two views. And in Darkei Moshe he further wrote a reason for those who practice baking on Yom Tov: for we say maror must be dipped in charoset because of kafa — meaning poison of lettuce. And he said there in this sugya kafa of all of them is hot — meaning poison of all vegetables, their medicine is hot; therefore they bake on the second night so the matzot will be hot and nullify the poison of maror — end quote from Eshel Avraham. And Darkei Moshe wrote: one may learn from this that it is good to keep the matzah hot if possible in order to be guarded from kafa — end quote. And Eshel Avraham's words siman 453 in this are astonishing, for he wrote: since there are poskim that flour in flour is called dry in dry, therefore one should bake everything before Pesach; you have no grain without wheat that sprouted except that they are nullified before Pesach; and since we hold dry in dry, it returns and awakens, therefore must bake before Pesach so it not return and awaken on Pesach at time of baking. And so in the name of Bach. And he wrote: one who is concerned for this stringency should not make a cooked dish from matzah on Pesach as he wrote from its baking. And those meticulous in baking before Pesach and on Pesach make a cooked dish from matzot — there is no reason for their words — end quote.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ד: And his intent is that in a cooked dish likewise it returns and awakens. On this Magen Avraham wondered: if so, even plain they are forbidden; and in this apparently the law is with Magen Avraham, but for another reason one should be stringent for a ba'al nefesh not to make a cooked dish from matzot on Pesach: for sometimes not all the flour is kneaded and mixed, and a little flour remains on the surface of the dough; and if it remained on the matzah above there would not be so much concern, for since it was given into the oven that little flour was scorched; and it is like flour of abshina, and in such a case where it is only a small amount one may be lenient. But sometimes that flour is in the middle of the matzah inside: for sometimes flour remains on the surface of the dough when it was a little hard, and by rolling afterward the helpers roll the pieces of dough to make matzah from them and by rolling it that flour comes inside the matzah. And in such a case Magen Avraham wrote siman 459, and especially siman 463 s.k. 4, to forbid putting into a cooked dish; and he left in doubt if they put it into the cooked dish whether to forbid; and he concluded one must forbid matzah in such a case since the matzah separates between the flour and the fire and it is not scorched. Therefore one does not dismiss one who practices this stringency.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ה: For the second night — see above siman 495 seif 6: on the 14th bread of hadra'ah, return bread is permitted; one may bake clean bread, for he can say "clean bread I want"; so too he can say "warm bread I want."
machatzit-hashekel/1:ו: That they practice to do so even though others remain, lest they were made by minors. He gives two reasons why one may bake: because of one matzah he lacks; although he has other matzot and could take the third lacking from those other matzot — nevertheless since they practice that the three matzot be from one tenth, and if he takes one from those other matzot the three matzot will not be from one tenth. And further lest those others were made by minors, and matzah for the mitzvah should not be made by minors as R' Moshe wrote end siman 464 as written siman 477; and if he forgot to eat afikoman and did not remember until after he blessed Borei Peri HaGafen on a cup in birkat hamazon, he should not eat afikoman and rely on matzah he ate during the meal etc.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ז: Regarding matzah d'oraisa etc. — and see siman 482. He meant: for from Torah a kezayit suffices, and he has two matzot remaining. Nevertheless in siman 482 there is a dispute among poskim how to conduct in such a case; therefore preferable to remove oneself from the dispute.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ח: For challah is forbidden etc. as written siman 457 seif 2.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ט: And then I will be able to see him and he will be there:
machatzit-hashekel/1:י: For in such a case according to everyone, even per Mordechai who brought there that it is permitted to bake and eat and leave enough for challah and leftovers — unlike Bach.
machatzit-hashekel/1:כ: And know what Magen Avraham wrote end siman 4: the time for its baking is at six; but Bach and Kaf HaChayyim who agreed with him wrote specifically at six and a half.
magen-avraham/1:_: After six hours. Even though the time of offering the Pesach is after six hours and a half, nevertheless its primary time is from midday, as Tosafot wrote Pesachim daf 5 and Yoma daf 28 and Niddah 63b. Tur wrote: the meticulous practice to bake everything before Pesach so that if something chametz becomes mixed it will be nullified — end quote; and it is obvious that when baked before Pesach and mixed in kneading, it is permitted afterward to cook the matzot on Pesach — for otherwise even to eat them plain is forbidden; and Eshel Avraham's words siman 453 in this are astonishing. Maharil wrote that some bake during the festival to eat fresh matzot every day; and Matanot Kehunah wrote: and the baker on the night of Yom Tov may not bake doubtful matzot; likewise forbidden to bake on the first night for the second night; however if he baked while still day on the first night he may say "I eat today warm bread" and may bake others on the first night, and what he baked while still day he hides for the second night — see above siman 407 seif 6. If one of the matzot was lost he may bake others on Yom Tov because of asmakhta that they practice to make three from one tenth, even though he has others, lest they were made by minors; and although for afikoman we rely on them (as written siman 477), for matzah d'oraisa we do not rely on them (Matanot Kehunah, Maharil) — and see siman 482. If dough was kneaded close to nightfall and he did not manage to bake until nightfall — uncertain if permitted to bake on Yom Tov so it not chametz, for challah is forbidden to bake so it not chametz; and one may say it is permitted to use a stratagem and say "I eat warm bread" as above, even though he will not take that dough for matzot, since he did not knead it for the mitzvah, nevertheless he may eat it during his meal or tomorrow on the first day — and see siman 406 seif 3 and what is written there.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) The practice etc. — it implies it is only a custom; and the custom is based because matzah eating is equated to the Pesach offering, as written "and you shall slaughter the Pesach to your God" etc. "seven days you shall eat matzot upon it" etc.; and we say: just as slaughtering the Pesach was after six, so making matzah for the mitzvah is after six hours; but from the essence of law the poskim proved one need not be concerned for this, for the primary hekesh is said regarding eating matzah on the first night that one be careful to eat before midnight like the Pesach that is eaten until midnight, as explained below siman 477; but not regarding making the matzah; and therefore b'dieved if he baked the matzah before six, and even a month or two months before Pesach, and made them for matzah, they are valid.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (b) We had to leave his duty in the first two nights, but the rest of the inventions do not take care of it:
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) Until after etc. — and see below siman 464 seif 3 what one must be careful regarding kneading at the time of the chametz prohibition. And behold most of Israel do not practice to be careful even regarding matzah for the mitzvah to knead on erev Pesach except some of them; and I searched among Acharonim and found in Bigdei Yesha a reason to advocate for the custom: because there are several views that even on erev Pesach in something, as explained above siman 452; and it is hard to be careful that they not find even something chametz in the wheat that is not sprouted; and therefore they bake beforehand so the chametz will be nullified. And in Ma'amar Mordechai I found he wrote: nowadays they are very lenient in the matter because of duress, except some who are careful in this to knead and bake after six the matzot with which one fulfills on the two nights; and so it is fit to do.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) Six hours — behold Kaf HaChayyim sides with Bach that specifically after six and a half; however in Magen Avraham and Eliyah Rabbah he sides with Shulchan Aruch that after six; and so ruled Beit Meir; and so implied in Biur HaGra. And know that from the law it is permitted to bake matzah on Pesach; however the meticulous practice to bake everything before Pesach so that if something chametz becomes mixed in them it will be nullified, unlike on Pesach where its prohibition is in any amount. And it is obvious that when baked before Pesach, even if there was something chametz in the flour, it already mixed and was nullified, and permitted afterward to cook the matzot on Pesach, for there is no chimutz after baking; and there are men of action who are stringent on themselves and do not soak and do not cook matzot on Pesach from concern lest a little flour remain inside the matzot internally that was not kneaded well and through soaking it will chametz; and see in Sha'arei Teshuvah siman 464 that from the law one need not be concerned for this, for we do not establish a prohibition presumptively, and especially nowadays when they practice to make thin wafers. Nevertheless one who practices this stringency one does not dismiss him; and see there who elaborated on this. Poskim wrote: the baker on the night of Yom Tov for matzah mitzvah should bake only what is needed for that night and not for the second night; however if he baked while still day on the first night he may say "I eat today warm bread" and may bake others on the first night, and what he baked while still day he hides for the second night; and Acharonim wrote that l'chatchila it is not worthwhile to bake on Yom Tov lest one come to ruin in separating challah on Yom Tov, and likewise in measuring flour and washing vessels, and lest the children sleep, and lest thereby one come to eat afikoman after midnight.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) Knead on erev Shabbat — meaning unlike those who are stringent to bake on the night of Yom Tov, as above at end of s.k. 4.
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: After six hours, remember the rest of the years:
turei-zahav/1:_: Knead on erev Pesach after six. Meaning after six and a half, for such is the time of slaughtering the Pesach; and not as some Geonim brought in Tur that one may bake only on erev Shabbat, and thus: therefore do not bake matzah except on erev Shabbat because of mar'it ha'ayin — if you bake from erev Pesach others will treat it lightly and be lenient; and although permitted to bake from erev Pesach, strengthen and adorn the mitzvah and bake in its time — end quote; and all this regarding matzah mitzvah. Beit Yosef challenged from what is written nevertheless he makes three matzot etc.: it appears his intent is in time of duress — meaning when there is fear to bake matzah properly, meaning all four together, for in this there is praise for matzah of the mitzvah as in chapter 5 Yom Tov; and this is impossible because of non-Jews who will notice if there is great smoke; nevertheless they make a small smoke on the night of Yom Tov only for the three matzot of Pesach; and thereby Beit Yosef's question is resolved. And this mar'it ha'ayin means others will think they eat on Shabbat also matzah; and afterward they wrote: and although permitted to bake it — meaning the three matzot of Pesach night alone, for in this there is no room for error; nevertheless because of the mitzvah in its time they bake on erev Shabbat; and Beit Yosef brought in the name of Mordechai: this mar'it ha'ayin means it will appear like preparing from Shabbat to Yom Tov — meaning on Shabbat forbidden to prepare and arrange the matzot on the table for the night as they do on weekdays, rather wait until night; and if he bakes the matzot on erev Pesach they will think he preceded himself in order to prepare tomorrow on Shabbat for Yom Tov to arrange the table — for otherwise why did he not wait also in baking matzot; and Beit Yosef explained another way which is strained; and Tur concluded in the name of R' Yehudah HaKohen: we have only the custom of our fathers to bake from erev Pesach and not to trouble on Yom Tov and after eating matzah; rather the zealous precede for the mitzvah — end quote; and as Shulchan Aruch ruled; and in my humble opinion another reason not to bake on the night of Yom Tov: there are many laws in baking challah as above siman 457, and not everyone knows the law thoroughly, and they will come to bake also on Yom Tov and not know the law of challah and come to transgress burning kodshim on Yom Tov; and I saw this stumbling block with my own eyes. And another reason: they hurry in eating so the children not sleep as written siman 493; and if he delays in kneading and baking certainly the children will sleep. And in Rokeach it is written to bake on the second night of Pesach because of love of the mitzvah that it is elevated thereby; and it is not proper to practice so in my humble opinion for the reason I mentioned; and see siman 495 in explanation of the words of Raavan who holds also one should not delay from eating immediately at night. Tur wrote: and I saw in Barcelona among the meticulous that they baked all they needed for the festival before the festival, so that if something chametz becomes mixed it will be nullified before its prohibition time — end quote; meaning before its prohibition in something — from the beginning of Pesach night; and so practiced Maharshal.
